entries.subject: A false color from three measured bands, as the HR 8799 planets have
entries.finding: Shown in infrared false color from its measured flux in F1550C 15.51 µm, F1065C 10.55 µm, F430M 4.278 µm (Sanghi et al. (2026), arXiv:2603.08787, with the MIRI fluxes of Matthews et al. (2024), Nature 633, 789). Sanghi et al. (2026) measured this planet with JWST/NIRCam in F410M and F430M, two of the three bands (F410M, F430M, F460M) that color HR 8799's planets; F460M is not measured. Its color is from the three bands it is firmly detected in, on its own range, so it is not compared with theirs.
entries.revisitWhen: Flux densities in three bands comparable with HR 8799's are published.

entries.subject: A second point source inside the planet's Hill sphere
entries.finding: Garza et al. (2026) find that a double point-source fit to the JWST/MIRI 15 micron image is preferred over a single one, most plausibly from systematics; follow-up would be needed to rule out a binary planet. Nothing is drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: Follow-up imaging confirms or rules out a companion of the planet.

entries.subject: The orbit of Matthews et al. (2026)
entries.finding: Matthews et al. (2026) refit the orbit with orvara using a third JWST position (2025 May 10) and publish medians only (a 20.9 au, e 0.244). Their medians miss both JWST positions by about 0.1 arcseconds, 6 to 10 of their errors, so they are not one orbit; Sanghi et al. (2026) publish their posterior, and its best sample is used.
entries.revisitWhen: A fit including all four JWST epochs publishes its posterior.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law fitted to the JWST/MIRI F1065C intensity PICASO 4.1 (Batalha et al. 2019, ApJ 878, 70) computes from Sonora Elf Owl cloud-free (Mukherjee et al. 2024, ApJ 963, 73; [M/H] +0.7, C/O 2.5 times solar, log Kzz 4) model atmospheres at 300 K and log g 4.25, read between the models spectra_logzz_4.0_teff_275.0_grav_100.0_mh_0.7_co_2.5, spectra_logzz_4.0_teff_275.0_grav_178.0_mh_0.7_co_2.5, spectra_logzz_4.0_teff_300.0_grav_100.0_mh_0.7_co_2.5, spectra_logzz_4.0_teff_300.0_grav_178.0_mh_0.7_co_2.5 (u1 0.497, u2 0.367; the law fits each model's eight angles within 0.38% of the centre): a cloud-free model, the one Sanghi et al. (2026), arXiv:2603.08787 fit to this planet, because no table reaches a planet this cold and nobody has resolved its disc. The temperature and gravity are that fit's (Table 5, Sonora Elf Owl, the lowest reduced chi-squared among the fits whose mass agrees with the dynamical mass: Teff 300 K, g 178 m/s2 (log g 4.25), [M/H] +0.7, log Kzz 4, C/O 2.5 times solar, radius 0.925, reduced chi-squared 2.62; [record](source/photometry/atmosphere-fit.json)), not the 275 K of its measurements record.
